preamble: In click loss, an alveolar click is replaced by a pulmonic velar stop: the anterior closure and the velaric suction are given up and the posterior velar closure is kept, together with the voicing of the accompaniment. The Eastern Kalahari Khoe languages of Botswana (Kua, Cua, Tsua) show this systematically, where conservative Gǀui keeps the click: voiced gǃ gives g, and nasal nǃ also gives g in many words (with loss of nasality). Traill and Vossen (1997) identify the alveolar click as the first to be replaced, by a velar, and Fehn (2020) reconstructs *gǃ > g alongside *ǃ > k and *ǃh > kh.

examples.note: Same reflex as in Kua and Tsua.
Nasal alveolar click replaced by a velar stop with loss of nasality; Kua has ŋabe.
Voiced alveolar click replaced by a voiced velar stop.
Nasal alveolar click replaced by g with loss of nasality; Kua has ŋaro. Chebanne lists this among cases of click loss without an evident phonological trigger.
